subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current-scope limits with plugin workarounds?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and sensitive data handling, and an open PR is already proposing new CLI/API surface for that policy.

options.title: Review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade/security review.

options.title: Ship reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress and size guidance, while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader native exclude-pattern tracker.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document current native backup limits and point users to plugin/workaround options such as KeepMyClaw only if maintainers decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: Gumadeiras is tied to both the original backup CLI review and the current backup infra extraction, making them the strongest code-history owner for the policy choice among the identified candidates.
